conclusions: Reject-domain retained: deduplicates bookmark URI strings and merges case-insensitive directory titles, not file bytes, decoded images or video sequences. No production port.

All14 original tests passed on current Python; no dependency adaptation or original source edits. They cover fixture loading, group retrieval, flattening, duplicate IDs and ordinary folder merge, not missing-ID preservation.

Authored finite control with two identical URI bookmarks and a third distinct URI, all without numeric IDs, loses the distinct bookmark: remove_from_tree matches None IDs. Original supplied fixtures also contain many nodes without IDs, but no claim every real Firefox backup has this form.

Authored finite control confirms same-name folders in different parents merge into the first folder; second parent becomes empty. README broadly promises same-name directory merging, so scope is observed policy rather than an asserted contradiction.
Positive distinct-ID control retains unrelated bookmark and removes later duplicate. URI equality is exact and folder matching uses lower(), with no URI normalization or Unicode casefold.
Unused get_id_path has mutable default list and returns list.append result on match; source-only observation, not executed. No performance or recursion-depth qualification.
File writer opens destination directly in write mode; no atomic replacement or recovery. No failure injection or user files touched.
Root MIT fully read; no additional differing license found among19files. CI lists Python3.3-3.6; current runtime run does not qualify those versions or actual Firefox restore.
